issue: What standard determines whether venue lies in a district for a federal wire fraud prosecution: must the wire transmission have a direct or causal connection to the misuse of wires, or may venue lie wherever the transmission originated, passed through, or was received?

sides.position: Venue for wire fraud lies only where there is a direct or causal connection to the misuse of wires; the counts may be prosecuted in a district where the relevant transmission originated, passed through, was received, or was orchestrated.
cases: United States v. Pace, 314 F.3d 344, 349-50 (9th Cir. 2002)
United States v. Jefferson, 674 F.3d 332, 368-69 (4th Cir. 2012)
United States v. Ramirez, 420 F.3d 134, 145-46 (2d Cir. 2005)
United States v. Johnson, No. 17-3776 (8th Cir. 2020)

quote: There is a circuit split regarding the standard to determine venue in wire fraud cases.
cite: United States v. Ronald David Johnson, No. 17-3776 (8th Cir. 2020)
